units.text: In regular expressions, the characters ‘⟦0⟧’ are ⟦1⟧special characters⟦2⟧ and have uses described below. All other characters are ⟦3⟧ordinary characters⟦4⟧, and each ordinary character is a regular expression that matches itself.
units.sourceHTML: In regular expressions, the characters ‘.?*+{|()[\^$’ are special characters and have uses described below. All other characters are ordinary characters, and each ordinary character is a regular expression that matches itself.

units.text: The period ‘⟦0⟧’ matches any single character. It is unspecified whether ‘⟦1⟧’ matches an encoding error.
units.sourceHTML: The period ‘.’ matches any single character. It is unspecified whether ‘.’ matches an encoding error.

units.text: A regular expression may be followed by one of several repetition operators; the operators beginning with ‘⟦0⟧’ are called ⟦1⟧interval expressions⟦2⟧.
units.sourceHTML: A regular expression may be followed by one of several repetition operators; the operators beginning with ‘{’ are called interval expressions.

units.text: The preceding item is optional and is matched at most once.
units.sourceHTML: The preceding item is optional and is matched at most once.

units.text: The preceding item is matched zero or more times.
units.sourceHTML: The preceding item is matched zero or more times.

units.text: The preceding item is matched one or more times.
units.sourceHTML: The preceding item is matched one or more times.

units.text: The preceding item is matched exactly ⟦0⟧ times.
units.sourceHTML: The preceding item is matched exactly n times.

units.text: The preceding item is matched ⟦0⟧ or more times.
units.sourceHTML: The preceding item is matched n or more times.

units.text: The preceding item is matched at most ⟦0⟧ times. This is a GNU extension.
units.sourceHTML: The preceding item is matched at most m times. This is a GNU extension.

units.text: The preceding item is matched at least ⟦0⟧ times, but not more than ⟦1⟧ times.
units.sourceHTML: The preceding item is matched at least n times, but not more than m times.

units.text: The empty regular expression matches the empty string. Two regular expressions may be concatenated; the resulting regular expression matches any string formed by concatenating two substrings that respectively match the concatenated expressions.
units.sourceHTML: The empty regular expression matches the empty string. Two regular expressions may be concatenated; the resulting regular expression matches any string formed by concatenating two substrings that respectively match the concatenated expressions.

units.text: Two regular expressions may be joined by the infix operator ‘⟦0⟧’. The resulting regular expression matches any string matching either of the two expressions, which are called ⟦1⟧alternatives⟦2⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Two regular expressions may be joined by the infix operator ‘|’. The resulting regular expression matches any string matching either of the two expressions, which are called alternatives.

units.text: Repetition takes precedence over concatenation, which in turn takes precedence over alternation. A whole expression may be enclosed in parentheses to override these precedence rules and form a subexpression. An unmatched ‘⟦0⟧’ matches just itself.
units.sourceHTML: Repetition takes precedence over concatenation, which in turn takes precedence over alternation. A whole expression may be enclosed in parentheses to override these precedence rules and form a subexpression. An unmatched ‘)’ matches just itself.

units.text: Not every character string is a valid regular expression. See ⟦0⟧Problematic Regular Expressions⟦1⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Not every character string is a valid regular expression. See Problematic Regular Expressions.
